missing_requirements.title: Atomic State Transition Guard for Ledger Settlement
missing_requirements.description: The payment processing service must enforce strict transactional atomicity and state machine guards (e.g., Pending -> Authorized -> Captured -> Settled / Failed) to prevent double-spending or unauthorized intermediate state updates.
missing_requirements.provenance: Double-entry bookkeeping and financial transaction integrity principles
missing_requirements.justification: Step 1: Financial ledgers require strict state machine transitions to prevent concurrent updates from moving a transaction from 'Failed' back to 'Authorized'. Step 2: Without explicit database-level isolation and state transition guards, race conditions under heavy load can lead to unverified state corruption or ledger imbalances. Step 3: Therefore, an atomic state transition invariant must be enforced at the database and application boundary to guarantee data integrity.

missing_requirements.title: Webhook Delivery Retry and Poison Message Isolation
missing_requirements.description: The system must guarantee reliable asynchronous webhook notifications for payment lifecycle events using an exponential backoff retry mechanism, coupled with a dead-letter queue (DLQ) for poison messages exceeding maximum retry attempts.
missing_requirements.provenance: Distributed systems and asynchronous event-driven architecture standards
missing_requirements.justification: Step 1: Payment processors must asynchronously notify downstream systems of state changes (e.g., charge success/failure). Step 2: Unreliable network conditions or failing downstream endpoints can cause message loss or endless retry loops that exhaust system resources. Step 3: Therefore, implementing bounded exponential backoff retries with dead-letter isolation is necessary to maintain system resilience and prevent processing bottlenecks.

missing_requirements.title: Cryptographic Audit Trail and Non-Repudiation Logging
missing_requirements.description: All payment request payloads, authorization tokens, state transitions, and cryptographic verification receipts must be logged to an append-only, tamper-evident audit log to ensure non-repudiation and regulatory compliance.
missing_requirements.provenance: PCI-DSS compliance and financial audit requirements
missing_requirements.justification: Step 1: Financial systems are subject to strict auditing and dispute resolution (chargebacks, fraud investigations). Step 2: Standard application logs can be altered or lack cryptographic chaining, failing to prove that transaction records were unmodified over time. Step 3: Therefore, an append-only audit trail with cryptographic integrity checks is mandatory to provide non-repudiation for all financial transactions.
